lessons.title: View Controller Lifecycle

quickCheck.prompt: Which method is called exactly once when the view controller's view is first loaded into memory?
quickCheck.explanation: viewDidLoad fires a single time after the view hierarchy is loaded. viewWillAppear and viewDidAppear fire on every appearance, and loadView is for creating the view itself — not responding to it being loaded.

options.text: viewDidLoad
viewWillAppear
viewDidAppear
loadView

lessons.title: Auto Layout & Constraints
lessons.body:
Auto Layout solves view positioning by satisfying a system of linear constraints at runtime, adapting to any screen size or orientation.

**Core concepts:**
- **NSLayoutConstraint** represents a linear equation: `item1.attribute = multiplier × item2.attribute + constant`.
- **`translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false`** — set this on any view you constrain programmatically, or you'll get conflicts.
- **Intrinsic content size** — views like `UILabel` and `UIButton` know their natural size from content.
- **Content Hugging Priority (CHP)** — how strongly a view resists growing *beyond* its intrinsic size.
- **Compression Resistance Priority (CRP)** — how strongly a view resists shrinking *below* its intrinsic size.
- **Ambiguous layouts** appear when constraints don't fully determine position or size. **Unsatisfiable layouts** occur when constraints conflict.

```swift
let label = UILabel()
label.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
view.addSubview(label)

NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
    label.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.leadingAnchor, constant: 16),
    label.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.trailingAnchor, constant: -16),
    label.centerYAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.centerYAnchor)
])
label.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(.required, for: .horizontal)
```

quickCheck.prompt: What property must you set to false before adding programmatic Auto Layout constraints to a view?
quickCheck.explanation: UIKit generates implicit constraints from a view's autoresizingMask unless you opt out. Setting translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints to false removes those implicit constraints so your manual ones can work without conflicts.

options.text: translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints
clipsToBounds
isHidden
autoresizingMask

lessons.title: Responder Chain, Target-Action & Delegation

quickCheck.prompt: Why should a delegate property be declared `weak`?
quickCheck.explanation: The delegating object is usually owned by its delegate (e.g. a VC owns its subview). If the subview held a strong reference back to the VC, both objects would keep each other alive indefinitely — a retain cycle. weak breaks the cycle.

options.text: To prevent a retain cycle between the delegating object and its delegate
Because delegates are value types
Because UIKit requires it for all properties
To improve performance

questions.prompt: What is the correct order of view controller lifecycle calls on first presentation?
questions.explanation: viewDidLoad fires once when the view loads into memory. viewWillAppear fires before each appearance, viewDidAppear after — the sequence is always load → willAppear → didAppear on first show.

options.text: viewDidLoad → viewWillAppear → viewDidAppear
viewWillAppear → viewDidLoad → viewDidAppear
viewDidLoad → viewDidAppear → viewWillAppear
viewWillAppear → viewDidAppear → viewDidLoad

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `frame` and `bounds`?
questions.explanation: frame locates the view in its parent's coordinate space. bounds describes the view's own coordinate space — its origin is usually (0,0) unless scrolled. Auto Layout works in bounds.

options.text: They are the same rectangle expressed in different spaces
frame is the view's rectangle in its superview's coordinate system; bounds is in the view's own coordinate system
bounds includes subviews; frame does not
frame is in points; bounds is in pixels

questions.explanation: Table views can have thousands of rows but only a dozen cells visible. Cell reuse pools off-screen cells and recycles them, keeping memory usage proportional to the visible area.

options.text: To prevent duplicate cell registrations
To reuse off-screen cell objects rather than creating new ones — saving memory and allocation cost
To guarantee cells are returned in insertion order
Because UIKit requires identifier registration

questions.explanation: The view hierarchy already retains subviews strongly. A weak outlet lets the VC reference the view without inflating its retain count — when the view is removed, it deallocates normally.

options.text: Because UIKit requires weak IBOutlets by Xcode convention
Because the view hierarchy holds a strong reference to subviews; a weak outlet avoids a retain cycle through the view controller
To improve rendering performance
Because strong IBOutlets cause memory leaks in all cases

questions.prompt: The main thread rule in UIKit means…
questions.explanation: UIKit was not built for concurrent access — modifying views from background threads produces unpredictable rendering artifacts or crashes. Always marshal UI updates to the main thread.

options.text: You should always use DispatchQueue.main.async for all UIKit calls
UIKit's view and layout systems must only be accessed from the main thread
Network calls must happen on the main thread
UIKit is thread-safe; the rule is advisory

questions.explanation: Priorities (1–1000) let Auto Layout gracefully resolve conflicting constraints. A required constraint (1000) must hold; lower priorities can be sacrificed to satisfy higher ones.

options.text: Determines which view is rendered on top (z-order)
Sets the strength of a constraint — lower priority constraints break before higher priority ones when there is a conflict
Controls how quickly an animation resolves the constraint
Defines which constraint is evaluated first during layout

questions.explanation: `layoutSubviews` is called by UIKit during the layout pass triggered by `setNeedsLayout` (deferred) or `layoutIfNeeded` (immediate). Override it to do custom subview positioning after bounds are known.

options.text: Only when you explicitly call it
Whenever the view's bounds change or `setNeedsLayout` is called, at the next layout pass
On every frame of the run loop
Only during initial view loading

questions.prompt: How does a touch event travel through the responder chain?
questions.explanation: The responder chain starts at the first responder (usually the hit-tested view), then moves up through the view hierarchy, view controllers, window, and application until someone handles the event.

options.text: From the window down to the first subview found
From the hit-tested view up through superviews toward the window and then the app delegate
Directly to the view controller regardless of view hierarchy
Through a shared UIApplication singleton

questions.prompt: What is the difference between UITableViewDelegate and UITableViewDataSource?
questions.explanation: DataSource answers 'what data to show' (numberOfRows, cellForRowAt). Delegate answers 'how to behave' (didSelectRowAt, heightForRowAt). Separating concerns lets you reuse the same data source with different interaction behaviors.

options.text: DataSource provides data (cell content, count); Delegate handles interaction (selection, row height, actions)
They are interchangeable — only one is needed
Delegate provides data; DataSource handles interaction
DataSource is for static tables; Delegate is for dynamic tables

questions.explanation: intrinsicContentSize tells Auto Layout the natural dimensions a view prefers based on its content (e.g. a label's text size). Content hugging and compression resistance work relative to this size.

options.text: Defining the minimum size a view should never go below
Communicating a view's natural size to Auto Layout based on its content
Setting the frame of a view programmatically
Overriding the bounds of a subview
